clue.text: Unexpectedly defeated and killed on sentry duty

definitions.meaning: beaten right at the finish line, idiomatically
shot dead (pipped) while standing guard at one's post

explanation.surface: A soldier's grim fate: surprised and shot while keeping watch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes losing narrowly at the last moment; read literally it means shot while stationed at a guard post.

clue.text: Such a complexion could be sweet

definitions.meaning: a fresh, rosy and creamy skin tone
a dessert of fruit with dairy topping

explanation.surface: Musing that a certain kind of skin might be described as lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a flawless rosy skin and also literally a fruit pudding served with dairy.

clue.text: Military band also incorporated into scheme

indicators.note: one word is taken inside another, as a member is brought into a body

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
also means too

explanation.surface: A regimental music group has been added to some programme too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but here it is a group of soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small unit of soldiers, a band in the sense of a company of people.

clue.text: Before climbing it, study vulcanology!

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, as in antenatal

explanation.surface: Advice to read up on volcanoes before tackling a famous mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'climbing' turns ANTE upwards to give the Sicilian volcano, which is just the thing a vulcanologist would study.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian mountain is an active volcano, a natural subject for anyone studying volcanoes.

clue.text: An idiot in Belgium

parts.note: a twerp is a silly or foolish person

explanation.surface: Someone foolish turns up in Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a location: the answer is a city found in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: The Flemish port city lies in northern Belgium, so it is a place in that country.

clue.text: Monotonous outside broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast as scattered far and wide, so the letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: An outside broadcast described as dull television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside broadcast' reads as a TV term, but 'broadcast' rearranges OUTSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and repetitive is wearisome, the sense of both words.

clue.text: Every single one is inside a church

indicators.note: the answer is sitting within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Every one of them can be found in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'insidE A CHurch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Each refers to every individual one of a group, taken separately.

clue.text: Eggs I serve in style. Cheers!

parts.note: ova is Latin for eggs

indicators.note: the letter acts as filling placed within another word

parts.note: ton means fashionable style

explanation.surface: A chef serving eggs elegantly, then a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers!' is the definition: applause rather than a toast. I goes inside TON, an old word for fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a round of applause and cheering from an audience.

clue.text: Our governors were both involved with the past

indicators.note: involved as entangled, so the letters are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: A remark that those ruling us were both tied up with history.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom refers to the people in authority, who govern us.

clue.text: Opposed to a Turkish commander this month

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman military officer
inst., short for instant, means of the current month in old letter style

explanation.surface: Resistance to an Ottoman officer at present.
explanation.definitionFit: To be against something is to be opposed to it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Order detectives to return to site of Turner collection

indicators.note: returning means the letters for the detectives are read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
the Tate gallery in London houses the bequest of J. M. W. Turner's paintings

explanation.surface: Police told to go back to a gallery holding Turner's paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate Britain gallery in London holds the Turner Bequest of paintings.
explanation.definitionFit: To dictate is to command or lay down orders authoritatively.

clue.text: Capital protection for a gunman

definitions.meaning: a covering for the head, capital meaning of the head
short for hoodlum, an armed gangster

explanation.surface: Armour for the city intended for a shooter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like a city or money, but it means 'of the head'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl covers the head, and in American slang the same word means a gangster.

clue.text: Hit the bottle back in the warehouse

indicators.note: back means the word for drinking heavily is read in reverse

parts.note: toped means drank heavily, as a toper does

explanation.surface: Someone drinking hard at the back of a storage building.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse or warehouse for goods.

clue.text: Attempt to comprehend Irish banking system

indicators.note: comprehend in its sense of include, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to understand how Irish banks work.
explanation.walkthrough: GIRO is a system of transferring money between bank or post office accounts, formerly common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A giro is a credit transfer system run by banks and post offices.

clue.text: Tree requiring a small enclosure

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a pen is an animal enclosure

explanation.surface: A sapling that needs a little fenced plot.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar with trembling leaves, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Colic is a recurrent complaint

definitions.meaning: ... in the sense of stomach pain, as in ... water

explanation.surface: A doctor's note that stomach pain is a chronic ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks medical alongside 'Colic', but in the second sense it is a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both intestinal pain and a moan someone keeps making.

clue.text: Parodies instruction to deliver drink

parts.note: to send is to deliver
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Satires include an order to have drinks brought over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'instruction to deliver drink' reads as an order: SEND SUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Sending something up means mocking it by imitation, which is what a parody does.

clue.text: "O day and night, but this is wondrous-!" (Shakespeare, Hamlet')

definitions.text: "O day and night, but this is wondrous-!" (Shakespeare, Hamlet')

parts.words: "O day and night, but this is wondrous-!" (Shakespeare, Hamlet')
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank: Horatio's line after seeing the Ghost, missing its final word meaning odd

explanation.surface: A quotation from Hamlet with its last word blanked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio says the line in Act 1 Scene 5 of Hamlet; Hamlet replies 'And therefore as a stranger give it welcome'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word means odd or unusual, matching Horatio's astonishment at the Ghost.

clue.text: Surely using an anti-perspirant is hassle-free?

definitions.meaning: a deodorant user would literally produce no perspiration
the idiom means no trouble at all

explanation.surface: A question about whether deodorant users have an easy time.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means easily done, and literally describes a dry, perspiration-free person.

clue.text: County people give support to retiring American female

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece holds the other up from beneath
retiring means going back, so the letters for American are turned round

parts.note: US is short for United States, American
folk is another word for people

explanation.surface: Locals back a shy American woman.
explanation.walkthrough: SUFFOLK is a county in eastern England. 'give support to' works because in a down entry the people sit beneath the reversed American and the female, holding them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffolk is an English shire on the North Sea coast, one of the counties of England.

clue.text: In a Prime Minister it reflects a chance for drum-beating

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister sees an opportunity to bang the drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflects' reverses IN A PM IT. 'drum-beating' suggests political trumpet-blowing, but literally the answer gives a percussionist something to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Kettledrums in an orchestra are the instruments a percussionist beats, offering the chance to hit drums.

clue.text: Bobby has debts in abundance

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer, a cop
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A policeman is deeply in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby' looks like a name, but it is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful, existing in large quantities.

clue.text: Splendid way to preserve wine

definitions.meaning: sealing bottles with a stopper keeps the wine

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent method of keeping wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective is dated slang for excellent, and the verb form means stoppering bottles.

clue.text: O to be in credit before the winter comes!

indicators.note: the words to be are placed inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A wistful wish to be financially sound as winter approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Browning's 'Oh, to be in England'. The definition describes a month preceding winter.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month falls in autumn, just ahead of the cold season.

clue.text: It serves food containing calcium and iron

parts.note: Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A diner whose dishes are rich in minerals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' is not a container here, just a link between the definition and the two symbols in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafe is a small restaurant, a place where meals are served.

clue.text: Army NCO cunning and quick witted

parts.note: SM stands for sergeant major, a non-commissioned officer
art can mean cunning or trickery, as in artful

explanation.surface: A sergeant described as crafty and sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart describes someone clever and mentally sharp.

clue.text: Scratch out a living

parts.note: the idiom for barely getting by, reread as an engraver whose trade is cutting marks into plates

explanation.surface: Getting by on very little money.
explanation.definitionFit: Engraving with acid or a needle scratches lines into a surface, so an engraver literally makes a living by scratching.

clue.text: Substance which is found in a high-performance car

indicators.note: found in means one word is located inside another

parts.note: GT stands for gran turismo, a fast touring car

explanation.surface: Some material discovered inside a sports car.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist is the essence or main substance of something.

clue.text: Manifest but quiet cry of pain

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
ow is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: An obvious but muffled yelp of hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: To manifest something is to display or make it visible.

clue.text: Strange objects, each containing toxic ingredients

indicators.note: containing means the word for each holds the other letters within it
ingredients are components mixed together, so the letters are blended into new order

explanation.surface: Weird items, every one with poisonous parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' looks like a link but is the container signal; 'ingredients' rearranges the poison word to OTIC before it goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Exotica are unusual or foreign things, curiosities from far away.

clue.text: Take up occupation — as a monk?

definitions.meaning: to live in or occupy a place
dressed in a religious robe, in a habit

explanation.surface: Is becoming a monk a career choice?
explanation.definitionFit: To inhabit is to dwell in somewhere, and split in two it describes wearing a religious robe.

clue.text: Lower production standards and add insult to injury

definitions.meaning: literally to manufacture goods of poorer quality

explanation.surface: A factory cutting quality and a bad situation turning nastier.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means aggravating trouble, and literally describes manufacturing poorer-quality goods.
